title: Failure of Unique Factorization in Z[√-5]

problemStatement.formal: In Z[sqrt(-5)], 6 has two genuinely different factorizations, 6 = 2*3 = (1 + sqrt(-5))*(1 - sqrt(-5)), witnessed using the norm a^2 + 5*b^2.
problemStatement.plain: Backfills metadata for the standard failure of unique factorization in Z[sqrt(-5)]. The Lean proof defines the ring and norm, verifies the two factorizations of 6, proves the relevant factors are nonunits, and shows the factorizations are genuinely different by a divisibility obstruction.
whyMatters: Z[sqrt(-5)] is the textbook example showing why unique factorization is special rather than automatic.
The norm calculation gives a concrete algebraic-number-theory route to irreducibility and nondivisibility facts.
This entry connects the fundamental theorem of arithmetic with the need for ideals or stronger hypotheses in general rings.

proven: `factorization_1` and `factorization_2` prove the two decompositions of 6 in Z[sqrt(-5)].
`two_not_unit`, `three_not_unit`, `one_plus_not_unit`, and `one_minus_not_unit` prove the listed factors are not units.
`two_irreducible` proves 2 is irreducible using norm constraints.
`two_not_dvd_one_plus` and `factorizations_essentially_different` show the factorizations are not the same up to the relevant divisibility relation.
